November 12, 2026, 14:00 UTC

### Agenda

1. Glamsterdam
	1. Execution layer EIP-8037/8038 issue (for info)

		- [ACDT](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2299) on Monday will discuss audit findings etc.
	1. Synopsis of Toni's testing on oversized/invalid ePBS payloads \[@nerolation]
	1. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5770 \[@jtraglia]
1. Recap of Devcon L1 R&D days \[@will-corcoran]
1. Open discussion of guiding questions arising from the workshop:
	1. What level of urgency should we have around the post-quantum and/or post-AI landscape?
	2. With Q1 in mind, what are our realistic options for accelerating the hardening of the consensus layer?
	3. With Q2 in mind, what information do we need in order to make sound decisions?
1. PFI EIP-8483 for Hegotá: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12609 \[@jtraglia]

For info: [Vote for a name for the I* upgrade](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/i-star-name-for-consensus-layer-upgrade-after-heze/26717)

### Signal which I-star name you prefer for the consensus layer upgrade after Heze
[For signalling purposes only, upgrade names are chosen by core devs]
https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/i-star-name-for-consensus-layer-upgrade-after-heze/26717

I would like to discuss including the Post-Quantum Material Registration EIP in Hegota:

* https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12609

I would also like to discuss the following PR for Glamsterdam. There have been some changes since we last spoke about it two weeks ago. Notably, there's a new `compute_execution_block_hash` function which uses RLP. I dislike having RLP leak into the consensus specs, but I believe this new check is important enough to justify it.

* https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5770

We shared our Ethlabs view on post-quantum and post-AI timelines and how we think we should prioritize accordingly [on ethmagicians](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/an-ethlabs-view-on-post-quantum-and-post-ai-timelines-pqai27/30351), and would like to briefly discus it tomorrow.

On agenda item 3: I think going straight to leanVM-based aggregation is risky. In the current leanSpec, the aggregation proof gates fork choice, finality and even block signatures, so a leanVM bug could compromise safety or halt the chain. I'd propose a hybrid transition instead. Validators sign every vote with both BLS and a PQ scheme. BLS aggregates stay authoritative for consensus, while PQ aggregates are produced and stored alongside them without being consensus-critical. That lets us test PQ aggregation at mainnet scale with no risk to the chain, before switching over in a later fork.

As discussed in our [ethmagicians post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/an-ethlabs-view-on-post-quantum-and-post-ai-timelines-pqai27/30351), we are withdrawing quick slots from Hegotá. Not sure this is the "official" way to do this 😅 I was only told to write here as an author and champion of the feature :)
